title: Delete the 25 fixtures that demand E0204 on Table E.1 primitives the LRM requires a SPICE-capable tool to accept
detail: VERIFIED. All 25 carry `//! reject module instantiation is not supported`. src/diag_code.zig:678-680 gives that title to E0204 with `.lrm = "6.2.2"` — VerA's flat-module limit, not any Annex E clause. E0204 is a class-2 (parser.zig) diagnostic: it fires on the instantiation form itself, before any primitive name, port name or parameter name is looked up, so none of the 25 pins one byte of Table E.1's content. Their single shared claim, 'VerA does not elaborate instances', is ALREADY recorded 9 times in tests/fixtures/ch06_hierarchy, which is where §6.2.2 belongs; nothing is lost by deleting these. A conformant Verilog-AMS compiler with hierarchy FAILS all 25, which is the definition of an anti-conformant fixture. 9 of them (primitive_discipline_unsupported, primitive_port_discipline_unsupported, primitive_mixed_discipline_override_unsupported, primitive_named_ports_unsupported, passive_named_ports_unsupported, spice_{passive,source,network,semiconductor}_primitives_unsupported) even say so in a header: 'DEBT — this rejection is NOT conformance. The LRM permits what VerA refuses here.' That header is itself stale: it directs the reader to `zig build ledger` and `tests/lrm-rules/`, and build.zig:69 records that torture.zig 'replaced conformance, exhaustive, sema.sh and ledger', while tests/lrm-rules/ does not exist. There is no verdict to annotate these with instead — tests/fixtures/README.md scopes `//! xfail` to the inverse case (LRM says error, VerA is silent) and makes it a hard fixture error without a `//! reject` to relax. Deletion plus the COVERAGE.md record of AE-13 is the only disposition that does not lie.
expected: 25 files removed. The Table E.1 name inventory they transcribed moves to the COVERAGE.md table of AE-13, which already carries it in prose at row `sE-3`.

title: All three Table E.2 limiter fixtures probe a module PORT, so VerA declines the $limit call and no algorithm is ever installed — they pass on a compiler that never heard of fetlim/pnjlim/vdslim
detail: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION. src/backend/cg_limit.zig:159-161 `writable(u)` returns `u != none_u32 and u >= num_ports`; :98-101 declines any call where neither probe net is writable. Each fixture writes `$limit(V(p), ...)` on a one-port module, so the pair is (port 0, global ground) and both are unwritable. Running `vera --emit-zig limit_fet.va` prints, in the generated device: `// §4.5.15 $limit DECLINED at 1 call site(s) ... $limit(V(p,0), "fetlim"): both nets are §6.5 ports, which the host masks`. limit_vds.va is worse: cg_limit.zig's `Alg` enum spells the drain-source limiter `limvds`, Table E.2 spells it `vdslim`, so `algOf` returns null at :183 and the call is dropped with no entry even in the declined list — `--emit-zig limit_vds.va | grep DECLINED` is empty. A declined $limit is the identity, so 'the limiter is transparent at the solution' is true by construction and the three CHECKs cannot fail. I confirmed the fix works: moving the probe to an internal net (`electrical mid; lim = $limit(V(mid), "fetlim", 0.7)`) makes 'fetlim' appear 3 times in the emitted device, i.e. the clamp is installed. NOTE on scope: E.3.4 calls Table E.2 'preferred names for three functions that MAY be available in a simulator', and §9.17.3 says 'If the string refers to an unknown or unsupported function, the simulator is responsible for determining the appropriate limiting algorithm' — so VerA spelling it `limvds` is NOT a conformance violation. The defect is fixture vacuity, not a VerA bug.
expected: Each fixture declares an internal net and probes it, so the call reaches the clamp list; the transparency claim survives unchanged but now rests on an installed limiter. limit_vds.va uses `"limvds"` with a header sentence recording that Table E.2's preferred spelling is `vdslim`, that §9.17.3 legalises declining an unrecognised string, and that E.3.4's preferred name is therefore unimplemented (row goes to COVERAGE.md). Add `//! lrm E.3.4` and `//! lrm 9.17.3` to all three.

title: $limit transparency is asserted to TOL 1e-12 on a V()-accessed quantity — 1e-12 is Annex D's CURRENT abstol; the Voltage abstol is 1e-6
detail: VERIFIED. The three `want` digits (0.3, 0.5, 0.4) are CORRECT and must not be touched — I re-derived each against SPICE's DEVfetlim / DEVpnjlim / DEVlimvds and each bias sits strictly inside every clamp branch, and the literals lens reached the same conclusion independently. Only the tolerance is wrong. §9.17.3 (docs/VAMS-LRM/ch9-system.html) promises only that 'the return value of the $limit() function is the value of the access function reference, WITHIN APPROPRIATE TOLERANCES', and adds 'In all cases, the simulator is responsible for determining ... what the return value is on a given iteration.' The LRM's only number for an appropriate tolerance on a Voltage-natured quantity is Annex D disciplines.vams `nature Voltage ... abstol = 1e-6` — I confirmed both constants in src/frontend/preprocessor.zig:1054-1085 (Current 1e-12, Voltage 1e-6). 1e-12 is six orders too tight and is literally the wrong nature's abstol. It passes today only because the call is declined (AE-02) and the harness imposes the bias exactly; a conforming simulator converging to its own vntol fails all three.
expected: TOL 1e-12 -> 1e-6 on the three CHECK lines, with a trailing comment naming it as the Annex D `nature Voltage` abstol. Land in the same pass as AE-02 to avoid touching the files twice.

title: Rejects a paramset, the exact mechanism E.4.2 names as the Verilog-AMS analogue of SPICE model binning
detail: VERIFIED. The file is `//! reject E0201` over `paramset annex_e_bin mosfet; parameter real l = 100n; endparamset`. E0201 is 'construct is not in the supported subset', .lrm = "C" (src/diag_code.zig:647-649) — VerA's Annex C subset limit, with no Annex E content. E.4.2 says the opposite: 'Similar functionality for Verilog-AMS is supported through use of the paramset, as described in 6.4 ... there may be several paramsets with the same identifier (name). The final determination of which paramset to use is made according to rules specified in 6.4.2.' A conformant compiler accepts this file and FAILS the fixture. It also asserts nothing about 6.4.2 selection even on its own terms. Same disposition as AE-01: the subset limit is already recorded by ch06_hierarchy/paramset_unsupported.va, paramset_overload_unsupported.va and paramset_output_unsupported.va, so deletion loses nothing.
expected: File removed; the E.4.2 gap becomes a COVERAGE.md row in AE-13.

title: Three fixtures reference SPICE objects (vertNPN, ecpOsc, VeRtNpN) that are never supplied to the harness, so every compiler errors and nothing is discriminated
detail: VERIFIED. torture.zig runs exactly one .va per fixture and has no concept of a companion SPICE netlist (tests/fixtures/README.md: 'No sidecar files'; the `//!` directive grammar in src/backend/tb.zig has bias/sweep/param/temp/time/wave/analysis/print and nothing else). E.2.1's rule is a two-step lookup — exact-case HDL match wins, else the mixed-case name matches SPICE regardless of case — and E.2.2.1/E.2.2.2 are worked examples over a `.MODEL` and a `.SUBCKT` that must exist. With no netlist, all three names are simply undefined and a fully conformant SPICE-capable simulator produces the same error. These are vacuous rather than anti-conformant (a correct compiler passes them), so they rank below AE-01, but they buy nothing and they are what COVERAGE.md rows sE-1-1, sE-2, sE-2-1, sE-2-2-1 and sE-2-2-2 currently cite as coverage.
expected: Three files removed. E.2.1/E.2.2 recorded in COVERAGE.md as blocked on harness capability (companion-netlist input), which is the honest state.

title: The chapter's only two legitimate rejects each contain a second `vsine` instance that raises the identical diagnostic, so neither can fail for the reason it names
detail: VERIFIED by reading both files. E.3.1 genuinely forbids these: 'Verilog-AMS HDL does not support the concept of passing an instance name as a parameter. As such, the following primitives are not supported: ccvs, cccs, and mutual inductors.' So `//! reject` is correct here and these two must be KEPT, unlike AE-01. But each body is `cccs f1(p, n, sense, 2.0);` (resp. `ccvs h1(...)`) followed by `vsine #(.dc(0.0)) sense(.p(p), .n(n));`, and E0204 fires on the vsine line too. Delete the cccs/ccvs line and the fixture still rejects, with the same substring — the reject is not attributable to the construct the fixture names. Remove the vsine instance. Honest ceiling, to be written in the header: even after the fix the diagnostic is the generic E0204 'module instantiation is not supported', so the fixture still cannot distinguish a tool that refuses cccs per E.3.1 from one that refuses all hierarchy per §6.2.2. Full discrimination needs a dedicated diagnostic code and is not this fixture's to buy.
expected: The trailing `vsine ... sense(...)` line deleted from both; `//! lrm E.3.1` added; header states the residual E0204 ambiguity and that the controlling-instance name is now a free identifier.

title: 'for other modules as well as the ports of all other modules it shall be ignored' — the one Annex E rule that is runnable today, and it is uncovered
detail: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION — I built VerA and ran the proposed fixture; it compiles clean and prints ok=1. E.3.2.1 ends: 'This attribute shall only apply to analog primitives or the ports of analog primitives; for other modules as well as the ports of all other modules it shall be ignored.' A plain behavioural module with `(* port_discipline="rotational" *)` on a port declaration is exactly 'the port of another module', so the attribute must change nothing. src/frontend/parser.zig:250 calls skipAttributes() at the head of every entry in parsePortList, so the syntax already parses; grep confirms VerA has no `port_discipline` handling anywhere in src/, which is precisely the behaviour the clause demands. This is the only Annex E rule in the whole chapter that needs neither elaboration nor a SPICE netlist, and it is worth more than the 25 files AE-01 deletes.
expected: `//! lrm E.3.2.1` + `//! bias V(p) = 1.25, V(n) = 0.0`; `module pd_ignored((* port_discipline="rotational" *) p, n); inout p, n; electrical p, n;` with `CHECKX("port_discipline on a non-primitive port is ignored", V(p, n), 1.25);` and `I(p, n) <+ V(p, n) / 1000.0;`. Confirmed output: `port_discipline on a non-primitive port is ignored got=1.25 want=1.25 ok=1`. Add a second variant with the attribute on the module item declaration (parser.zig:298) if a second point is wanted.

title: An under-argumented $limit is silently DECLINED instead of diagnosed, though 9.17.3 makes the extra arguments REQUIRED — a real xfail with source evidence
detail: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION. §9.17.3: 'Two additional arguments to the $limit() function ARE REQUIRED when the second argument to the limit function is the string "pnjlim"' and 'One additional argument ... IS REQUIRED when the second argument ... is the string "fetlim"'. cg_limit.zig:102-105 instead does `if (d.args.len < 2 + n) { try decline(..."too few arguments for the algorithm named"); continue; }` — and `decline` only appends to a list that codegen.zig renders as a COMMENT in the emitted device (cg_limit.zig:209-212). No diagnostic, no non-zero exit: I ran `vera --emit-zig` on `$limit(V(mid), "fetlim")` and got RC=0 with the decline note buried in a comment. Both fixtures must probe an INTERNAL net or the port rule of AE-02 declines them earlier and they prove nothing. GUARD, honoured here: §9.17.3 also says 'If the string refers to an unknown or unsupported function, the simulator is responsible for determining the appropriate limiting algorithm' — so an unknown algorithm string is legal and nobody may write a reject for it.
expected: Two fixtures, each `//! lrm 9.17.3` + `//! lrm E.3.4` + `//! reject` + `//! xfail VerA declines an under-supplied $limit instead of diagnosing it`. (a) `electrical mid; lim = $limit(V(mid), "fetlim");` (b) `... $limit(V(mid), "pnjlim", 0.026);`. They register as XFAIL now and become a hard XPASS FAIL the day VerA diagnoses it, which is the point of the verdict.

title: `mutual_inductor` is a spelling no clause of Annex E defines, so the reject is indistinguishable from 'undefined module'
detail: VERIFIED. E.3.1 says 'ccvs, cccs, and mutual inductors' in prose only; Table E.1 has no mutual-inductor row, and no clause anywhere in docs/VAMS-LRM/annex-e-spice.html gives the construct an identifier. The fixture instantiates `mutual_inductor k1(p, n);` — a name the suite invented. Since VerA rejects every instantiation, the reject would be identical for `foo k1(p, n);`. The requirement is real and worth keeping, but the fixture must not imply the LRM supplied the name. Lower than AE-06 because there is no second-instance confound here.
expected: Header records that E.3.1 names 'mutual inductors' in prose with no identifier, that `mutual_inductor` is this suite's own spelling, and that the reject therefore attaches to the E.3.1 requirement only by convention. Add `//! lrm E.3.1`.

title: The third CHECK divides two constants asserted two lines above, and `//! temp 400` affects no assertion despite a header paragraph claiming it discriminates tc1/tc2
detail: VERIFIED. Line 32 pins `r == 1000.0` with CHECKX; line 36 pins `V(p,n) == 1.0` with CHECKX; line 37 then asserts `V(p,n)/r == 1e-3`, which is 1.0/1000.0 — bit-identical to the literal 1e-3 — once the two lines above pass. The digits are right (Table 2-1 gives k = 1e3; §2.6.2 uses `7k` as its example), so nothing here is a wrong literal. The `//! temp 400` on line 27 reaches no assertion: the module declares no tc1/tc2 and no assertion reads $temperature, so lines 21-24's claim that a build 'that kept a temperature coefficient in scope would drift off it at 400 K' is unbacked — this module has no temperature term for a coefficient to live in. And the fixture cannot test E.3.3's actual rule ('a module or paramset defined in the Verilog-AMS will always be selected in favor of a SPICE primitive, model, or subcircuit using exactly the same name'), because it reads no stamped flow and there is no competing SPICE `resistor` in the harness to lose the race. Keep it — it is one of only five runnable files and its CHECKX on `r` is genuinely well-derived — but stop it claiming E.3.3.
expected: Delete line 37 or downgrade it to CHECKEQ; delete `//! temp 400` and the paragraph it supports; retitle the header to what it actually pins (2.6.2 scaled-literal default and §3.4 parameter defaulting on a module NAMED `resistor`), and add a one-line note that the E.3.3 selection rule itself is unreachable without SPICE-netlist input. Cite `//! lrm 2.6.2`, not E.3.3.

title: The second CHECK is titled for 6.3.6 flow scaling it never observes; the first CHECKX is the only real claim in the file
detail: VERIFIED. Line 19's `CHECKX("$mfactor at the top of the hierarchy", $mfactor, 1.0)` is correct and well-derived from Table 9-29 ($mfactor resolves as $mfactor_specified * $mfactor_hier, empty product at the top) — keep it verbatim. Line 23's `CHECK("one device carries the unscaled flow", $mfactor * V(p), 2.0, 1e-15)` is titled after 6.3.6 rule 1, 'All contributions to a branch flow quantity in the analog block shall be multiplied by $mfactor', but the contribution on line 24 is `V(p) + 0.0 * $mfactor` and no assertion ever reads a stamped residual. With line 19 already pinning $mfactor to 1.0 bit-exactly, line 23 degenerates to a restatement that the `//! bias V(p) = 2.0` directive arrived — a claim line 19 is not making but which is worth far less than its title. I checked whether the scaling could be observed in-language and it cannot: $mfactor is applied at contribution time and the testbench exposes the residual only in its dump, not to CHECK. So there is no rewrite that rescues the title. (Correcting the literals lens slightly: line 23 is not strictly tautological, since V(p) is pinned by the directive rather than by an earlier CHECK — the defect is the false 6.3.6 label, not unfalsifiability.)
expected: Delete line 23 and the lines 20-22 comment block that justifies it; keep line 19 and its Table 9-29 derivation. Add `//! lrm E.4.1` and `//! lrm 9.18`. Do NOT cite 6.3.6 — nothing in the file observes it.

title: Zero of 37 fixtures carry a `//! lrm` cite, so the chapter contributes nothing to `zig build torture -- --coverage`
detail: VERIFIED: `grep -c '//! lrm' *.va` returns 0 for every file. tests/fixtures/README.md makes `//! lrm` the suite's only mechanical coverage backing — 'zig build torture -- --coverage prints every cited section, sorted, with the fixtures citing it ... it makes the cited set greppable, diffable and countable, which is the only mechanical backing a chapter is covered claim can have' — and a failing fixture prints its cites so the report names the RULE, not just the file. Annex E is currently invisible to that. Cheapest high-leverage change in the chapter and it changes no verdict. Fold into whichever pass touches each file (AE-02, AE-06, AE-09, AE-10, AE-11 already specify their cites).
expected: Every surviving .va gains at least one `//! lrm <section>` naming the clause it actually pins — not the clause its filename suggests. After AE-01/04/05 that is 9 files: 3 limit_*, mfactor_subcircuit, spice_name_shadow, unsupported_cccs, unsupported_current_controlled, unsupported_mutual_inductor, plus the new port_discipline_ignored_on_module and the two AE-08 fixtures.

title: COVERAGE.md maps 22 Annex E clauses onto fixtures that only prove VerA emits E0204, and must become the honest record of what is blocked and why
detail: VERIFIED row by row. Row `table-e-2` claims 'exact fetlim/pnjlim/vdslim names and arguments' is covered by the three limit_*.va — AE-02 proves none of the three installs an algorithm. Rows `sE-2-1`, `sE-2-2-1`, `sE-2-2-2` cite the three files AE-05 deletes. Rows `sE-3`, `table-e-1` and the two Table E.1 rows cite the 25 files AE-01 deletes. Row `sE-3-2-2` admits 'requires elaborated connectivity' and cites a fixture anyway. This item is the SINK for the ~20 lens findings that are genuinely uncovered but not writable: after checking each against the harness I found they all reduce to two blockers, not twenty pieces of work. BLOCKED ON MODULE INSTANTIATION (E0204/§6.2.2): every Table E.1 behaviour equation; E.3's ordered PARAMETER association; E.2.2.1's 3 mandatory bjt ports and 1 optional `s`; Table E.1's required port/parameter names and positional arity; E.3.2's three-level precedence; E.3.2.1's three value rules (string / declared discipline / domain continuous) on a primitive; E.3.2.2's compatible / error-per-3.11 / electrical-fallback trio; E.3 final paragraph's paramset over diode/bjt/jfet/mesfet; E.4.2 binning; E.4.1's $mfactor as an instance property; E.2.2.1/E.2.2.2's unconstrained instance-name first letter; E.2.2.3's ecpOsc translation. BLOCKED ON HARNESS (no companion SPICE netlist): E.2.1's exact-case-wins direction and its case-insensitive fallback; E.3.3's 'shall issue an warning' for a module shadowing a SPICE model/subcircuit, and the may/shall split against the primitive half. NOT BLOCKED, being written: E.3.2.1's ignore rule (AE-07) and §9.17.3's required $limit arguments (AE-08). Also park the derived Table E.1 digits here so no one re-derives them — I recomputed and confirm every one: vexp branch 3 at t=5n with (dc,val0,val1,td0,tau0,td1,tau1)=(0,0.25,1,1n,1n,3n,2n) is 0.4761225125107178 (V_td1 = 1-e^-2 = 0.8646647167633873); vpulse mid-fall at 4.5n with td=1n,rise=1n,width=2n,fall=1n is 0.5 exactly (t2=4n, t3=5n); vpwl with wave '{0,0,1n,1,3n,-1} holds -1.0 at t=5n rather than extrapolating to -3.0; vsine with freq=fmmodfreq=1e8, fmmodindex=0.5, ampl=2 gives exactly -2.0 at t=10n, a sign flip against the +2.0 an FM-ignoring implementation returns; resistor with r=1k,tc1=1m reads 1/1300 = 0.0007692307692307692 under absolute T=300 or 1/1099.85 = 0.0009092148929399465 under T-300.15 at temp 400 — the reading must be stated, it is not settled by Table E.1. Also record E.3.4's preferred name `vdslim` against VerA's `limvds` (permitted by §9.17.3, but the preferred name is unimplemented).
expected: Table rebuilt: one row per HTML section id, each either naming a surviving fixture that pins real content, or saying BLOCKED with the blocker named. The boundary-disclosure paragraph is rewritten to say the diagnostics proved parser reachability and nothing about Table E.1, instead of the current 'every Table E.1 row now contains executable named-port and named-parameter syntax'.

title: 32 dead `.expected-error.txt` sidecars that the README forbids and the runner never opens
detail: VERIFIED. tests/fixtures/README.md opens with 'No sidecar files' and 'there is no second file to drift out of step with it'; build.zig:69-71 records that torture.zig replaced the three sidecar formats the old runners needed. `grep -n 'expected-error' tests/torture.zig build.zig` returns nothing — they are never read. 31 contain the string 'module instantiation is not supported', 1 contains 'E0201'. CORRECTING THE WEAK LENS: its claim that 'one already drifted to a different form' does not hold — I compared every sidecar against its file's inline `//! reject` line and all 32 match byte for byte. The item survives on the README rule alone, so it is cosmetic. AE-01/04/05 remove 29 of the 32 as collateral; this item sweeps the remaining 3.
expected: No `.expected-error.txt` remains under tests/fixtures/annex_e_spice/. Worth a repo-wide `find tests/fixtures -name '*.expected-error.txt'` in the same pass.
